limitation.note: The public API behaves differently from v2 here. v1 REST contacts lack the audit fields created_by_id, updated_by_id, created_time, and updated_time. Object Query contacts include those audit fields. The remaining differences between the Object Query contact shape and the full v2 contact output are: v2's null custom-field handling, the other_phone_type enum mapping, and per-field projection semantics. Use the public contact fields available in the Object Query REST expansion for standard contact data. Object Query GraphQL (public, undocumented; evidence is source-observed) can provide parity; see the shared GraphQL parity reference entry GP-3.

Take the record from the operation's successful JSON response and build the `custom_fields` object. Always build the object: it is `{}` when the row has no custom fields. Use the `customFields` array when the row has one, otherwise the `custom_fields` array; turn each `{key, value, type}` entry into `key: value` (when a key appears more than once, the last entry wins). Then convert `long` and `number` values to numbers, convert `boolean` values to true or false, and leave other types unchanged; null values stay null. If the row has neither array, collect every property whose name ends in `__c` into the object; an empty array gives `{}` and the `__c` properties are then not used. Include `custom_fields` only when it was requested.
